name: flat_grid_block_to_expert_lookup
description: For per-expert kernels on unbalanced MoE workloads, use a flat grid sized to the ACTUAL per-expert work sum with a block_to_expert lookup tensor — NOT a (G, max_per_group, ...) grid which wastes dispatches.
preconditions: Per-expert operation where per-expert work count varies
Unbalanced MoE real traces (e.g. tokens-per-expert range 0..16000+)
steps: Host-side: compute work_per_expert = (M_g + GROUP - 1) // GROUP (or whatever per-expert unit)
total_work = work_offs[-1].item() — one CPU sync, negligible
In kernel: expert_g = tl.load(block_to_expert_ptr + pid_flat); work_base = tl.load(work_offs_ptr + expert_g); local_idx = pid_flat - work_base
Eliminates ALL wasted dispatches; unbalanced MoE with giant experts no longer pays for (G × max_sg) blocks
expected_impact: On gpt_oss_20B unbalanced MoE (M_g range 105..16053): switched 723K wasted dispatches -> 2K exact dispatches. Wgrad quant bwd: 12.77 ms -> 6.85 ms (~1.9x). General pattern applicable to any per-expert grouped op.
decision_rules: Use whenever the per-expert work distribution has variance >2x.
Even on balanced workloads the flat-grid form is no worse — and the code generalises for free.
